title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S is a commutative ring. A = S{X_0, dX_0} is the free divided-power (PD) de Rham complex of the PD affine line over S. In degree 0 it is the PD polynomial algebra S⟨X_0⟩ with basis X_0^{(i)}. In degree 1 it is S⟨X_0⟩·dX_0, with (dX_0)^2 = 0 and d(X_0^{(i)}) = X_0^{(i-1)} dX_0. The augmentation α: A → S kills every X_0^{(i)} with i ≥ 1 and kills dX_0. S itself is viewed as a differential PD ring with d_S = 0 and its own PD structure, and α respects these structures.

Problem. Grothendieck classifies endomorphisms φ of A that are
- unital S-algebra maps,
- commute with d (φd = dφ),
- preserve the augmentation (αφ = α),
- but are not required to respect the divided powers.

Grading is not required either: he writes φ(X_0^{(i)}) = ξ_i = A_i + B_i dX_0 with A_i, B_i in S⟨X_0⟩. So φ may mix degrees 0 and 1, i.e. it is an endomorphism of the underlying 'super' algebra commuting with the odd derivation d.

Step 1: φ on dX_0. φ(dX_0) = dξ_1 = dA_1 = A_1' dX_0, because d(B_1 dX_0) = 0.

Step 2: the even parts A_i. From φd = dφ, A_i' dX_0 = dξ_i = φ(X_0^{(i-1)} dX_0) = ξ_{i-1}·A_1' dX_0 = A_{i-1}A_1' dX_0. Augmentation gives α(A_i) = 0. In S⟨X⟩, d: S⟨X⟩^+ → S⟨X⟩dX is bijective (X^{(n)} ↦ X^{(n-1)}dX). So by induction A_i is the unique augmentation-zero antiderivative of A_{i-1}A_1', which is A_1^{(i)}. Hence A_i = A_1^{(i)} with A_1 ∈ S⟨X_0⟩^+.

Step 3: claimed classification. Grothendieck concludes, in a box, that φ corresponds bijectively to data (A_1 ∈ S⟨X_0⟩^+, B_i ∈ S⟨X_0⟩ for i ≥ 1) 'sans autre condition'.

Step 4: PD-compatible case. Using the PD structure in which (dX_0)^{(n)} = 0 for n ≥ 2, one has (A + B dX_0)^{(i)} = A^{(i)} + A^{(i-1)} B dX_0. So φ commutes with divided powers iff ξ_i = ξ_1^{(i)} for i ≥ 2, i.e. B_i = A_1^{(i-1)} B_1. The PD-compatible endomorphisms are then parametrised by the pair (A_1, B_1).

Purpose. This is a computation of the endomorphism monoid of the 'PD de Rham line', presumably towards understanding automorphisms and functoriality of PD de Rham complexes for the 1976 IHÉS talk. In modern terms it describes maps of the odd tangent bundle of the PD line commuting with the de Rham differential.
errors: The boxed claim that the B_i are arbitrary 'sans autre condition' is wrong in general. φ must respect the multiplicative relations X^{(i)}X^{(j)} = C(i+j,i) X^{(i+j)}. Applied to ξ_iξ_j this forces A_iB_j + A_jB_i = C(i+j,i) B_{i+j}. For S torsion-free (e.g. i = j = 1: 2A_1B_1 = 2B_2) this pins B_{i+j} down, so over a Z-torsion-free or Q-algebra base everything is determined by (A_1, B_1). The B_i become largely independent only in positive characteristic: over an F_p-algebra the generators are the X^{(p^k)}, so roughly only the B_{p^k} are free. The PD-compatible formula B_i = A_1^{(i-1)}B_1 does satisfy these relations, consistent with the final statement.
The page does not check that the A_i-part is compatible with the multiplicative relations; it is, since A_i = A_1^{(i)} satisfies them automatically. So the error concerns only the B_i.
Minor: the transcribed 'α : A_1 → S' is presumably α : A → S.

ideas.what: Classification of augmented differential-algebra endomorphisms of the PD de Rham complex of the PD affine line, allowing degree-mixing (non-graded) maps
ideas.modern_name: Endomorphisms of the dg (super)algebra Ω of the PD line; maps of the odd tangent bundle ΠT commuting with d (Q-manifold morphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in supergeometry (e.g. Kontsevich, Ševera for ΠT and End(R^{0|1})); unsure for the PD setting

ideas.what: Even part of φ forced to be A_1^{(i)}, using bijectivity of d on augmentation ideal of S⟨X⟩ (PD Poincaré lemma)
ideas.modern_name: PD Poincaré lemma / uniqueness of PD antiderivatives

ideas.what: PD-compatibility criterion B_i = A_1^{(i-1)}B_1 for degree-mixing endomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: PD structure on a graded-commutative algebra with odd generators

missed.claim: Grothendieck considers non-graded endomorphisms of the PD de Rham complex commuting with d, i.e. treating Ω as a supercommutative algebra with an odd derivation. Odd parameters B_i appear alongside the even substitution A_1. This anticipates the supergeometric view of de Rham complexes (ΠT, End(R^{0|1})-actions) in a PD/crystalline context. The PD-compatible maps are parametrised by (A_1, B_1).
missed.quote: On cherche les endomorphismes φ de S-algèbre différentielles à augmentation (et à p.d. sans p.d. !) ... φ(X_0^{(i)}) = ξ_i = A_i + B_i dX_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Degree-mixing symmetries of PD de Rham complexes relate to recent work on the PD/sharp line G_a^♯ and stacky approaches to de Rham and crystalline cohomology. It is a minor historical precursor, not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine scratch computation with one error (the freeness of the B_i). The only mildly notable feature is the deliberate consideration of degree-mixing endomorphisms, a supergeometric viewpoint, of the PD de Rham complex.
transcription_corrections: 'A = S{X_0}, dX_0}' should read 'A = S{X_0, dX_0}'.
'α : A_1 → S' is likely 'α : A → S'.
'i.e. avec une pu[?] les p.d.' is likely 'i.e. avec [ses / une structure de] p.d.'.
Neighbouring 'pages' supplied are from an unrelated typescript (SGA 7 IX, Néron models); the handwriting is overwritten on the reverse of that typescript.
